disputes.issue: E4 claimed Arts was within 0.3 days of non-Arts in every category with 50+ tickets, which contradicts E5 (on-site hardware: Arts 6.5 vs main campus 1.8; Arts has ~700 such tickets). The residual-gap attribution to on-site coverage also lacked a direct mechanism measure, leaving association-only arguable.
disputes.resolution: E4 now restricts parity to remotely handled categories, notes on-site hardware is reported separately, and adds Arts non-SlotBook median excluding on-site hardware (3.1 days). E5 adds time-to-technician-arrival (Lindqvist 4.7 vs main 0.6 days) with similar repair time. Expected answer kept causal; rationale updated.

disputes.issue: H1's first clause ('generally slower to resolve Arts tickets than equivalent tickets') is literally true for on-site hardware (6.5 vs 1.8), so supported/unknown was arguable for the conjunction.
disputes.resolution: H1 reworded to the faculty-attribution claim (slower because they come from Arts), which E4/E5 (Education parity on the same campus) contradict. Expected kept contradicted; rationale updated.

disputes.issue: 'Arts Faculty leadership' was undefined; if the Operations Manager is not leadership, the Dean's denial plus no emails make 'contradicted' defensible.
disputes.resolution: H4 now defines leadership as the Dean or the Faculty Operations Manager. Expected kept unknown.

disputes.issue: Same leadership ambiguity in R4's antecedent: the Dean herself was evidently not told, making association-only arguable.
disputes.resolution: R4 'from' reworded to match H4 (neither Dean nor Operations Manager informed), whose truth state is unknown. Expected kept unknown; rationale updated.

disputes.issue: E14 gave September 2024 keyword count 74 vs a 31/month baseline (2.4x seasonal ratio) against 241/134 (1.8x) in 2025, implying no SSO-specific excess and making 'contradicted' arguable.
disputes.resolution: September 2024 keyword count changed to 58 (about 1.9x), so seasonality is comparable and neither supports nor refutes an SSO effect. Expected kept association-only; rationale updated.

disputes.issue: Rationale claimed the transfer would worsen service for non-Arts users, but if Arts' 3,870 tickets leave the central desk its load per FTE falls (7,990/19 vs 11,860/21); the proposal's scope (all Arts tickets or not) was also unspecified, making 'premature' arguable.
disputes.resolution: A5 now states the Arts desk takes over all Arts tickets. Rationale rewritten around the Arts desk being several times overloaded (about 1,935 tickets/FTE vs 565 centrally at 94% utilisation). E3 added to required evidence. Expected kept harmful.
